output.summary: A tall biennial or short-lived thistle native across most of Europe, western Asia and northwestern Africa. Its stems have spine-tipped wings, and it bears pink-purple flower heads rich in nectar. Young taproots can be eaten raw or cooked, and peeled stems may be steamed or boiled.
output.edibilityNote: Young taproots are eaten raw or cooked; peeled stems are steamed, boiled or used cleaned in Iranian thistle-stem stew.
